  - text: CLASS 9 · QUADRILATERAL PROOFS
  - heading "Converse of Midpoint Theorem" [level=1]
  - paragraph: "Objective: Use a line through one midpoint parallel to a second side to prove it bisects the third side."
  - text: 30 min RIGOROUS PROOF INTERACTIVE
  - navigation:
    - button "Interact"
    - button "Learn"
    - button "Example"
    - button "Formula"
    - button "Practice"
  - main:
    - heading "DRAG · EXPLORE · PROVE" [level=2]
    - complementary:
      - heading "What can you do" [level=3]
      - list:
        - listitem: Drag A, B, or C to reshape the triangle.
        - listitem: Point D is locked as the midpoint of AB.
        - listitem: Rotate line DE. When DE ∥ BC, AE = EC.
      - heading "Show / Hide" [level=3]
      - checkbox "Show midpoints" [checked]
      - text: Show midpoints
      - checkbox "Show lengths" [checked]
      - text: Show lengths
      - checkbox "Show parallel guide" [checked]
      - text: Show parallel guide
      - heading "Mode" [level=3]
      - button "Forward (DE ∥ BC)"
      - button "Converse (Test)"
      - heading "Line DE" [level=3]
      - text: Rotation 0°
      - button "Rotate DE counterclockwise":
        - img
      - slider "Line DE rotation": "0"
      - button "Rotate DE clockwise":
        - img
      - button "Reset":
        - img
        - text: Reset
    - article:
      - img "Draggable converse midpoint theorem triangle": A B C D E A (2, 6.395) DE ∥ BC
      - text: AD
      - strong: "3.80"
      - text: DB
      - strong: "3.80"
      - text: AE
      - strong: "5.00"
      - text: EC
      - strong: "5.00"
      - complementary:
        - heading "Results" [level=3]
        - text: AE / EC = 1.000
        - strong: ✓ Bisected!
      - img
      - text: DE ∥ BC (parallel)
    - article:
      - heading "Why it works" [level=2]
      - paragraph: "By the Converse of the Midpoint Theorem:"
      - paragraph: If a line is drawn through the midpoint of one side of a triangle and is parallel to a second side, then it bisects the third side.
      - strong: D is midpoint of AB and DE ∥ BC ⇒ AE = EC
    - article:
      - heading "Worked Example" [level=2]
      - paragraph: "Given: D is the midpoint of AB. A line through D is drawn parallel to BC, meeting AC at E."
      - paragraph: "To Prove: E is the midpoint of AC."
      - list:
        - listitem: AD = DB.
        - listitem: DE ∥ BC.
        - listitem: By the converse theorem, line DE bisects AC.
      - text: Therefore, AE = EC. Hence proved.
    - article:
      - heading "Common Mistake" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: Common Mistake
      - paragraph: Thinking that passing through the midpoint is enough, even if the line is not parallel.
      - img
      - paragraph: Here DE is not parallel to BC, and AE ≠ EC. Parallelism is an essential hypothesis.
    - article:
      - heading "Your Challenge" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Rotate line DE away from parallel and observe the ratio. Then restore parallelism to prove the theorem.
      - text: × Not parallel
      - strong: AE / EC = 0.873
      - text: ✓ Parallel
      - strong: AE / EC = 1.000
      - button "Check Parallelism":
        - img
        - text: Check Parallelism
      - text: The midpoint converse is verified.
